sample_size.excerpt: We used a nested case-control design to compare the fatty acid compositions in plasma from 120 men who later developed prostate cancer with 120 matched controls who did not.
sample_size.location: Abstract, methods; total_n derived from reported group counts 120 + 120 = 240

cases.excerpt: We used a nested case-control design to compare the fatty acid compositions in plasma from 120 men who later developed prostate cancer with 120 matched controls who did not.

effect_size.excerpt: Conditional logistic regression models were used to obtain odds ratio estimates while adjusting simultaneously for the effects of one or more potential confounders. The relative risks (RRs) of prostate cancer for men in successively higher quartiles of plasma alpha-linolenic acid level were 3.0 (95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.2-7.3), 3.4 (95% CI = 1.6-7.5), and 2.1 (95% CI = 0.9-4.9), compared with those with levels below the detection threshold (P trend = .03).

headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 5 studies yielded an effect size of 1.15 (95% CI: 0.92–1.43), indicating no statistically significant association between alpha-linolenic acid and prostate cancer\aggressive. Although the point estimate suggests a potential positive relationship, the confidence interval includes the null. These findings were accompanied by very high heterogeneity (I² = 77.16%), reflecting highly inconsistent results across studies.
